Years ago, MacBooks came with a slot that allowed you to secure your laptop to a table leg or similar using a cable lock. Such devices were most useful in coffee shops, so you didn't have to take your laptop with you when you went back to the counter to order another drink.

Those slots have long disappeared, but now you can buy adapters to add a security lock to your MacBook Neo, MacBook Air, or MacBook Pro...

You have to be a long-time MacBook user to remember the design with an embedded security slot on the side of the machine. These slots were designed for T-shaped accessories; insert the accessory into the slot and turn it 90 degrees to lock it. The most common design is a cable loop that can be threaded through a table leg in a coffee shop or library.

CompuLock has now revived this concept, launching adapters that can be installed on the corners or edges of a MacBook to attach a cable lock. The adapters use a two-piece design that clamps onto the MacBook with screws.

The company has now added a version for the MacBook Neo, in addition to the original MacBook Air and MacBook Pro models.

It must be emphasised that this type of lock has always been only a low-security device, intended merely to prevent someone from snatching your MacBook and running off in the space of a few seconds. Personally, I feel at ease using it in smaller coffee shops, because I can still see my table when I go to the counter for another tea, but I would never rely on this kind of lock to let my MacBook out of my sight.

These adapters are not cheap at $70, since you still have to buy the lock itself, but if you happen to have an old lock in a drawer, you might think it's worth getting it out again.
